issues.title: Unjustified division by the indicator in the eigenvalue-derivative lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims an explicit quotient for every covered continuously differentiable real-eigenvalue point, but the proof at real nonzero \(\kappa_p\) establishes only \(I(p)\kappa_p'=\frac12\kappa_p\int_D n_p'|w_p|^2\). The zero-over-zero case is admissible: on \(D=(0,1)\), take the constant parametrization \(n_t\equiv9\), \(\kappa_t\equiv\pi\), \(v_t(x)=\sin(\pi x)\), and \(w_t(x)=\sin(3\pi x)/3\). These functions satisfy both PDEs and both transmission boundary conditions, while \(I(t)=1/2-9(1/9)(1/2)=0\), \(n_t'=0\), and \(\kappa_t'=0\). Thus the old right-hand side is undefined as 0/0.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's explicit derivative formula is undefined for allowed zero-effect parametrizations; only the product balance is universal. The later bifurcation-order theorem and radial propositions use regimes where the indicator is nonzero away from the exceptional point, so their formal conclusions remain established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the universally valid balance identity I(p)\kappa_p'=\frac12\kappa_p\int_D n_p'|w_p|^2, and give the displayed quotient for \kappa_p' only under the additional condition I(p)\neq0. When I(p)=0, retain the balance identity without claiming that it determines \kappa_p'. No downstream result requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: The proof unjustifiably divides by a quantity that can vanish, so this is not merely transcriptional. However, conditioning the quotient on a nonzero denominator while retaining the valid identity in the zero case is a short, routine, source-supported repair. It preserves the explicit derivative formula throughout the regular regime, and the exceptional case does not propagate to any listed dependent result.

issues.title: Annulus indicator proof integrates over the excluded disk core
issues.failure_explanation: The first polar-coordinate expression for I(p) integrates the v_p contribution over 0<rho<1 even though the integration domain is the annulus r<rho<1. It therefore adds the excluded inner disk and does not imply the subsequent formula containing the lower-boundary terms at rho=r.
issues.overall_effect: As typeset, the proof contains a false domain integral and a gap between that line and its endpoint evaluation. Replacing the lower bound restores the proposition's indicator formula and its subsequent uses without changing the result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the lower limit of the radial integral for the v_p contribution from 0 to r, so that it is integrated over [r,1], and then apply the stated Bessel-product identity. The proposition and its conclusion remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old source itself uniquely forces the lower limit r: D is explicitly the annulus B_1\setminus\overline{B_r}, the w_p term is integrated from r to 1, and the immediately subsequent endpoint formula contains the boundary terms at r. Thus the 0 is a transcriptional lower-bound error that an intended reader can correct without supplying a new premise or repairing the mathematical argument.
